source: M5 Forecasting competition (University of Nicosia / Makridakis Open Forecasting Center); data provided by Walmart
download_note: Original data is Kaggle-hosted and requires a Kaggle account + acceptance of the competition rules. This copy was obtained from Nixtla's public redistribution (github.com/Nixtla/m5-forecasts) used by their MIT-licensed open-source forecasting tooling. No authentication or access restriction was bypassed. Verify the M5 competition terms before any redistribution of your own.
license: M5 competition data (Walmart). Use governed by the M5 Forecasting competition rules. Nixtla redistribution is under the Nixtla project's MIT license for tooling; the underlying data terms are unchanged.
citation: Makridakis, S., Spiliotis, E., & Assimakopoulos, V. (2022). The M5 competition: Background, organization, and implementation. International Journal of Forecasting, 38(4), 1325-1336. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2021.07.007
country_context: United States (Walmart stores in California, Texas, Wisconsin)
business_domain: Big-box grocery/hobby/household retail; daily unit sales at item x store granularity
date_range: 2016-05-22 (d_1941; exact range written to processed/ by the adapter)

processed_subsample.selection: deterministic: top-40 (item_id x store_id) by total units over the full training window; seed 42
processed_subsample.days_per_series: full training window (d_1 ... d_1941) after trimming each series' leading all-zero warm-up
processed_subsample.reason: raw is ~58M long rows / 237MB sell_prices; a 40-series slice keeps the processed CSV small and gives each series a long history for lag/rolling features

known_limitations: US big-box retail - not representative of Indian SMEs or of small-business retail.
No marketing-spend field; the adapter holds marketing_spend at 0 (not invented).
promotion_flag is held at 0. M5 has calendar events and SNAP flags, but neither is a promotion; mapping them to promotion_flag would be a fabricated relationship, so it is not done.
sell_prices are per wm_yr_wk (weekly); the adapter forward-fills weekly price to daily.
Only a 40-series deterministic subsample is materialised (full M5 is available in raw/ for anyone who wants it).

MAPE is unreliable for this dataset: many days have zero unit sales, so per-point percentage error is undefined/exploding. MAE and RMSE are the meaningful forecasting metrics here (both are recorded).
